requirements.requirement: opsadmin user exists on node1 with the specified ed25519 public key installed for SSH access
requirements.summary: opsadmin did not exist before (cmd-e73bea8f82314eb5). It was created (cmd-0e43719bc99e4fd6), and the exact given ed25519 key was written to /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership and permissions (0700 dir, 0600 file) (cmd-20363c4fb6444e39). The key content was re-verified unchanged after the restart (cmd-469acb6ab5024348).

requirements.requirement: SSH access to node1 requires key-based authentication (password/interactive auth disabled system-wide, and opsadmin has no usable password)
requirements.summary: Existing config had no conflicting overrides (cmd-cc20d402138348fa, cmd-db3840aa98244e51, cmd-75c2133ea5e94ecd). A drop-in (00-key-only.conf) was added disabling PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication while keeping PubkeyAuthentication yes, validated with sshd -t, and applied via reload (cmd-1407232a5864457d, cmd-2ae7c52e0c514e61). sshd -T confirms the effective settings both before and after the restart (cmd-2ae7c52e0c514e61, cmd-469acb6ab5024348). No active Match blocks override this (cmd-f787396bf4ff4b72). opsadmin's password was locked ('!!' in shadow) both before and after restart, eliminating password login for that account specifically (cmd-046c0046e63340c0, cmd-5689d886f5e642d4, cmd-d350cf52a0374e94, cmd-469acb6ab5024348).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task were achieved and directly verified: opsadmin was created with the exact specified public key installed correctly, and SSH access now requires key-based authentication (password and keyboard-interactive auth disabled via an sshd_config.d drop-in, plus the opsadmin account's password locked). The mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 31b01b46...), a deferred reboot acknowledgement, a connection-timeout during the transition, a new post-restart boot_id (8fbebb86...), and full recovery of sshd, the opsadmin account, and the key-only SSH configuration afterward.
limitations: A small leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the restart-evidence reboot trigger was not cleaned up; this is low-risk and does not affect SSH functionality.

No live SSH login attempt (with the private key or a password) was captured, so authentication behavior is inferred from sshd -T effective configuration and shadow/authorized_keys state rather than an end-to-end connection test.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task (user creation, key install, password lock, sshd drop-in, reload) or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol (baseline capture, deferred reboot, post-restart re-verification). No troubleshooting dead-ends or unrelated mutations were found. One minor residue: the deferred-reboot trick left /tmp/reboot.log on the node (visible in the after-executor temp-files snapshot, created by cmd-503816ca9b384623's `>/tmp/reboot.log` redirection); it is tiny, non-sensitive, and a natural byproduct of the mandated restart evidence collection, but it was not cleaned up afterward.
